correctness.rationale: With h=n−1 the indexed windows of any circular host trace a closed walk on the full binary shift graph. Subtracting one copy of each required edge leaves integral flow with supply on legal vertices that start in 1 and end in 0, and demand on those that start in 0 and end in 1. The initial run length r at a supply vertex forces at least r shifts before reaching any demand vertex, even along forbidden edges. Appending r ones reaches the legal demand vertex 0u1^r from 1^r0u and is bijective by peeling the full trailing run of ones at the destination. Legal vertices are strongly connected via the all-ones vertex; the augmentation is therefore Eulerian and gives an avoidance-preserving cover. Independently, counting a supply vertex with a marked initial one is equivalent to counting a supply vertex of some length k from 2 to h by deleting the ones before the mark. There are F_(k−1) such vertices: for k≥3 they have the form 1w10, with w any valid (k−3)-word; k=2 gives one. Hence the excess is sum_{k=2}^h F_(k−1)=F_(h+1)−1, also zero at h=1. The mandatory count F_(n+2) gives the stated Lucas identity. The source scripts were inspected, not executed; their finite checks are not the all-n proof.

evidence: Resultary 475811a7997d supplies the generating function for the optimal excess under cyclic avoidance. At q=r=2 the excess series is z/[(1−z)(1−z−z²)], giving F_n−1 in coefficient n−2.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general indexed result specializes exactly to the same excess. Contracting each forbidden cyclic run of the distinguished letter to length r−1 preserves legal windows by keeping their allowed entrance and exit segments, so the host constraint is inessential even for that general class. The generic Eulerian Extension formulation alone does not imply the closed form.

In a full-graph covering walk the potential telescopes against exactly the prior required-arc imbalance because new, illegal vertices have no required arcs. evidence: 115d2faf86fa states F_(n+2)+F_n−1 for cyclic 11-avoiding hosts covering every linearly 11-avoiding n-word, n≥2. Bit complementation converts both language and host to the 00 formulation.

The full-domain reduction is valid for cyclic hosts: a legal window of length n≥2 meets a nontrivial zero run only by using one exposed end of the run as a window endpoint. Collapsing the run retains the corresponding zero adjacent to its neighboring one. No legal window crosses that run. There is at least one one in a cover. Thus all required windows survive even for a run spanning an arbitrary cut in the circular representation.

originality.rationale: The earlier Oct. 18 indexed result computes the identical cyclic-host optimum under a host avoidance constraint, after bit complementation. Its proof uses a leading-symbol potential whose one-step inequality in fact holds on every edge of the full de Bruijn graph. Therefore its identical lower bound extends directly to unrestricted hosts, with zero mandatory imbalance at newly allowed vertices. Independently, contracting every maximal cyclic zero run to a single zero maps any unrestricted cover to an avoiding cover without losing a required window. The enlarged optimization domain consequently gives the same theorem by a direct reduction, not a distinct extremal fact.
residual_risks: The classic Edmonds–Johnson and Hsu full texts were inaccessible on the routes tried; no negative inference about those papers is made. That limitation does not weaken the explicit earlier indexed implication. No historical priority outside the checked sources is asserted.
